newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican ruling party dooms petrochemical sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Mexican ruling party dooms petrochemical sell-off.

text.p: Ruling party nationalists have doomed government plans to privatise Mexico's 61 petrochemical plants by voting at a convention to formally oppose the sell-off.

Delegates of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which has governed Mexico since taking power in 1929, took the historic vote late on Saturday by rising to their feet, clenching fists and shouting nationalistic slogans.

"Mexico, Mexico, Mexico" cried the ecstatic PRI delegates at the party's 17th National Assembly when a proposal for the PRI to defend the petrochemical industry as state property won a favourable vote.
The decision should oblige PRI congressmen, who control Mexico's congress, to block the privatisation which has already been delayed by charges the move is unconstitutional.
Since former President Lazaro Cardenas nationalised the oil industry in 1938, the petroleum sector has been a focal point of nationalistic sentiment.
Privatisation of petrochemcial plants has come up against stiff opposition, stopping the government from pushing through the sale of a complex of ammonia plants in Cosoleacaque.

National and international companies, including Terra and Farmland of the United States and Mexico's Agrimex, have already placed bids for Cosoleacaque, which has annual sales of more than $400 million. The winner of the auction should have been named back in April.

The oil and gas industry comes under the state-owned monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), easily Mexico's largest company and a source of massive support for the PRI via the powerful oil workers' unions.
